page: UpCloud PREMIUM-80xCPU-512GB is a Premium family cloud server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, delivering 80 vCPUs across 80 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.4 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 500 GB local SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in multi-core CPU execution, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also rank in the top tier, alongside cached small-block read memory bandwidth. Large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth, single-core CPU performance, and database operations fall within the strong top 25% tier. However, memory performance under Passmark is average, and LLM text generation speeds for both small and medium models are weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention despite the high physical core count. Qualitatively, the server offers high resource density with a massive memory footprint and high core count, making it a cost-efficient option for parallelizable workloads that do not require dedicated CPU pinning. It is highly suited for software compilation, multi-threaded data processing, static web serving, and database operations, while being less optimal for LLM text generation tasks.
